title: Cunningham's Fig: Old White Figs You Can Visit
meta_description: A strangler fig from India to northern Australia. Queensland's Curtain Fig is 500 years or more, Palermo's has a 10 m trunk, and Hong Kong's spreads 34 m wide.
intro: Ficus virens, the white fig or Cunningham's fig, grows wild from India through South-East Asia to northern Australia, and often begins life high in another tree as a strangler. The Curtain Fig in Queensland's Atherton Tableland is the clearest case: its aerial roots drop about 15 metres in one hanging wall, and the Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service puts it at 500 years or more. Palermo's register gives the white fig of Villino Favaloro a trunk 10 metres round, in a city better known for its Moreton Bay figs. Hong Kong Park's Tai Chi Garden has one 20 metres tall and 34 metres wide, a native that drops its leaves. In Brisbane, two stand on Eagle Street beside a banyan, planted in 1889, and a hollowed one at Newstead House is believed to be 200 years old.
